In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MRP logic is not robust to workload variability.
MRP is a good idea, but it needs to be implemented in a way that is consistent with the plant's environment.

MRP systems can be made to work well if the master schedule is smooth, if component lot sizes are small, if the bill of material structure is not too complex, if leadtimes are short, if the routing is not too complex (i.e., if there is a dominant path), if capacity is flexible, and if the capacity slack is small.

the best MRP performance occurs with an efficient, well-designed manufacturing system.
